headline.text: Päijät-Häme's crude recorded MDT meeting share of 0.3% (95% CI 0.1–1.1; n=2/659) lags the national 6.0% (893/14873), though this reflects recording practice rather than care.

details.text: In Päijät-Häme, the crude curative treatment share is 29.6% (95% CI 26.2–33.2; n=195/659) compared with 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, so the 95% confidence interval includes the national value and is not distinguishable from it.

Across overlapping treatment categories where a patient can have several treatments within 12 months, Päijät-Häme's crude shares exceed national values, with 95% confidence intervals excluding the national benchmark for life-prolonging treatment at 44.5% (95% CI 40.7–48.3; n=293/659) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) and symptomatic treatment at 50.8% (95% CI 47.0–54.6; n=335/659) versus 39.5% (5871/14873).

For recorded multidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings, Päijät-Häme's crude share is 0.3% (95% CI 0.1–1.1; n=2/659) and its 95% confidence interval excludes the national value of 6.0% (893/14873), but HILMO captures specialist procedures only from direct patient contacts, so MDT records measure recording practice rather than care.

While public county data do not report when treatment starts, preliminary national figures show lung cancer care in Finland averages 155 days from first symptoms to first treatment versus 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark, comprising 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care.

headline.text: Päijät-Häme's crude 17.8% (95% CI 15.0–20.9) share with no treatment record within 12 months is below the national 27.5%, while crude shares lack age and stage adjustment.

details.text: The category 'no treatment record within 12 months' mixes untreated patients and unrecorded treatment; because Päijät-Häme's crude share of 17.8% (95% CI 15.0–20.9; n=117/659) has a 95% confidence interval entirely below the national 27.5% (4089/14873), this is consistent, as an inference rather than a finding, with relatively complete treatment recording.

Taulukko 11 county shares are crude with separate limitations: they are not age-adjusted, since county age-adjusted shares appear only in Kuva 16 (with digitised national curative lines, precision ±0.5 percentage points, at 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women), and separately they cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

A journal article found that hospital discharge register (HILMO) diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, but this concerns diagnosis concordance only and says nothing about how completely treatment, referral, or MDT is recorded, while national lung cancer data reporting, collection, and storage remain incomplete.

Public data do not measure symptom onset, referral dates, or county timing for the first specialist visit (recorded within 12 months for 93.6% nationally) or treatment start; primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, and imaging appears only indirectly as clinical-only diagnosis in about 20% of patients.

headline.text: The team recommends auditing recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding, tracking access times under THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions, and standardising referrals and diagnostic coordination.

details.text: Given Päijät-Häme's crude 0.3% (95% CI 0.1–1.1; n=2/659) recorded MDT share versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally and about 48% missing stage at diagnosis nationally, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT meetings while reading gaps as data-quality signals, since Finland lacks a cancer quality registry and uniform recording instructions are needed.

Because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and national pathway monitoring is lacking, the team recommends reporting referral-to-treatment access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions (covering 16 cancers) with handover alerts; the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with recommended time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Since referrals follow local instructions and mentor insight notes a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating, the team recommends a referral template and persistent-symptoms rule after a normal X-ray (as in KYS's pathway document) plus a diagnostic-phase contact person; the STM roadmap (measure 1.2.3) plans care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 for county adoption by 2029–2031.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
